hints.title: Structural Identity Obstacle
hints.text: Why does flattening trees to traversals risk ambiguity when duplicate values or structural differences exist? How can comparing corresponding nodes recursively determine structural identity?

hints.title: Recursive Mirror Invariant
hints.text: Two binary trees are identical if and only if their root values match and their corresponding left and right subtrees are identical.

hints.title: Recursive Validation Procedure
hints.text: If both nodes are null, return true. If exactly one is null or their values differ, return false. Otherwise, recursively verify that left subtrees match and right subtrees match, returning their logical AND.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: number of nodes in tree p (0 <= N <= 100)
M: number of nodes in tree q (0 <= M <= 100)
complexity.notes: Simultaneous recursion visiting each corresponding node at most once with call stack bounded by tree height.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Comparing node counts or single traversals without null markers can falsely equate structurally different trees.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recursive call stack requires O(H) auxiliary memory, optimal for structural comparison.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Handling null base cases cleanly before dereferencing node values.
